messages.author: 09607d3641d0afd1
messages.subject: Re: Error
parts:
Kristen:

You're not having very good luck getting Distance to do your bidding.  At what point in the project creation process does this happen?  Is it before you get to interact with the software; I mean is this in reaction to any input you have provided?  If so, then perhaps Distance didn't load properly and you might need to reinstall Distance.

On the other hand, if the error is in response to some input you have provided, then possibly the first part of the message "Text property is read only" might indicate that you have provided input Distance did not expect. 

Can you provide more information about when the error arises?

messages.subject: Re: Error
parts:
I've some some good days with program Distance doing my bidding! This seems strange since I was using Distance problem-free last week. I click on the Distance symbol on the desktop. It opens, and I click the "new project" icon in the upper left. I name it and place it in a folder I would like, after which it goes to the selection page where I click "analyze a survey that's already been completed." Now the error message pops up. Strangely, I can open any project that already exists and make changes without errors. 

I also have a side question if you have time: I calculated detection probabilities for all of my bird species using Distance. I selected to appropriate models (only using the 4 recommended in Johnson et al. 2010) based on AICc and GOF. However, some of the detection probabilities are less than 0.1, many near 0.01. When I apply these probabilities back to month-by-month raw detections to generate estimated abundances per month, the events where I have to apply a 0.01 probability of detection results in astronomical and basically impossible species abundances. Is this just an artifact of trying to fit mathematical models to human observation patterns, or is there another criteria with which I could assess my models? Right now I can't justify selecting a different model with a delta AICc of hundreds even though it makes more biological sense...

Thank you,
